text: Each full or model-only gate invocation shares one TLC budget across all its checks (#497). Discovery reads the selected Docker daemon's CPUs and memory, reserves a quarter of the memory, and allows at most one 2 GiB container per CPU and per available 2 GiB; a smaller machine gets one container scaled down, and failed discovery gets one 1 GiB container. invariant verify -tlc-parallel can only lower the count. Every TLC container has an explicit memory limit, no extra swap and a Java heap of three quarters of the limit. A cancelled check that is still queued starts no container, time limits start at admission, and a slot is held through cleanup and a stall retry. Java heap or GC exhaustion is a named operational failure, never counterexample evidence, and exit 137 says the check was killed with possible memory exhaustion. Until now the gate started every check at once, and a big model's checks ran the machine out of memory (#445).
